sets.relationshipLabel: a performer and the tool of their trade
sets.explanation: A singer needs a microphone and a drummer needs drumsticks — each performer is defined by the instrument that makes their part possible.

sets.relationshipLabel: moments that bookend a live show or a recording
sets.explanation: Load-in opens the physical setup and load-out closes it, just as fade-in opens a track's sound and fade-out closes it — matched bookends at two different grains of a performance.

sets.relationshipLabel: two instrument parts defined by touching, one setting the other vibrating
sets.explanation: A reed only sounds when it touches the mouthpiece, and a string only sounds when the bow touches it — each pair is a contact point that creates the vibration.

sets.relationshipLabel: a public cover concealing the true identity or sound
sets.explanation: A stage name hides the birth name and Auto-Tune hides the raw voice — both pairs trade a polished public surface for the truth underneath.

glossary.definition: A thin strip of material, often cane, that flexes to make sound in some wind instruments.

definitions.definition: Someone who performs music with their own voice.
A device that picks up sound so it can be heard louder or recorded.
Someone who plays the drums, keeping the beat for a band.
The pair of sticks used to hit a drum kit.
The process of bringing all the gear into a venue before a show.
Packing up and hauling all the gear out after a show ends.
When a sound or track starts quiet and slowly gets louder.
When a sound or track gets quieter and quieter until it's gone.
A thin strip of material, often cane, that flexes to make sound in some wind instruments.
The part of an instrument you put to your mouth to play it.
A stick strung with hair, drawn across strings to make them sound.
A thin stretched wire or cord on an instrument that vibrates to make a note.
The made-up name a performer uses in public instead of their own.
The name someone was given at birth, before any public persona.
Software that corrects or smooths out a singer's pitch electronically.
The natural sound a person makes when they speak or sing.
